note: One message in a chunk a server streams to a watching client (see spec/spectating.md), for a 4.17 client. Chunks hold records back to back. A record can leave out its command and shorten its time and object to a difference from the record before it; spec/spectating.md says how a reader recovers them.

bits.name: channel
bits.note: The channel the message went on.

bits.name: sizeIsByte
bits.note: Set where the body's size is one byte.

bits.name: objectIsDelta
bits.note: Set where the object is a difference from the last record's.

bits.name: commandRepeats
bits.note: Set where the command is the last record's and is left out.

bits.name: timeIsDelta
bits.note: Set where the time is a difference from the last record's.

fields.name: time
fields.note: When the message was sent, in seconds of the stream's clock.

fields.name: timeDelta
fields.note: When the message was sent, in milliseconds after the last record's time.

fields.name: size
fields.note: How many bytes the body occupies.

fields.name: byteSize
fields.note: How many bytes the body occupies.

fields.name: object
fields.note: The network object the message's header names.

fields.name: objectDelta
fields.note: The network object the message's header names, as a difference from the last record's object.

fields.name: body
fields.note: The rest of the message, after its command and object.

fields.name: byteBody
fields.note: The rest of the message, after its command and object.
